item.title: Financial transactions watchdog steps up action against money service businesses
item.description: Canada’s financial intelligence agency revoked the registrations of 82 money service businesses in 2025-26, up from 12 the previous year.
item.dc:creator: The Canadian Press
item.content:encoded: OTTAWA — Canada’s financial intelligence agency revoked the registrations of 82 money service businesses in 2025-26, up from 12 the previous year. The Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre (FINTRAC) says it focused significant resources on the money services sector in the last year due to money laundering and terrorist financing risks associated with such businesses. FINTRAC notes in its annual report that businesses which exchange foreign currencies, transfer money, cash money orders or traveller’s cheques, or deal in virtual currency must register with the centre before offering these services. Individuals convicted of certain offences are ineligible to register a money service business, meaning a registration could be denied or revoked. The report says the centre took “aggressive action” to address non-compliance in the sector, including illicit cryptocurrency activity, across Canada in the last year. In addition to rescinding registrations, Fintrac imposed administrative monetary penalties totalling more than $198 million on nine money service businesses for a variety of violations. --- Jim Bronskill, The Canadian Press This report by The Canadian Press was first published Oct. 26, 2026.

item.title: WestJet signs codeshare partnership deal with Qatar Airways
item.description: WestJet says it has signed a codeshare partnership with Qatar Airways that will make it easier to travel to Doha.
item.dc:creator: The Canadian Press
item.content:encoded: CALGARY — WestJet says it has signed a codeshare partnership with Qatar Airways that will make it easier to travel to Doha. Under the agreement, WestJet will start by placing its airline code on Qatar Airways’ non-stop flights to Doha from Toronto and Montreal. Passengers travelling on codeshare itineraries will benefit from co-ordinated connections, the ability to earn WestJet loyalty rewards on their full trip and through-checked baggage. Qatar Airways will place its code on select WestJet-operated flights from Toronto and Montreal. The agreement will allow Qatar Airways passengers to connect to 11 Canadian destinations, including Vancouver, Calgary, Edmonton, Halifax, St. Johns, N.L., and Winnipeg. WestJet says it plans to place its code on select destinations beyond Doha as part of a future phase. --- This report by The Canadian Press was first published Oct. 26, 2026.
